evidence: Caes. BC 2.10: super laterēs coria indūcuntur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The accusative serves for lying on top and for putting on top alike; poets also use the ablative. For plain “on”, Latin says in with the ablative: in mēnsā.

evidence: Cic. Div. 1.48: in summā columnā (Lewis & Short, s.v. superus)
terms.comment: Latin names the top as part of the thing: in summā columnā, on top of the column.

evidence: Caes. BG 4.17: īnsuper bipedālibus trabibus immissīs (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: aliīque super aliōs et jūmenta in hominēs occiderent
phrases.english: and they fell on top of one another, and the pack animals onto the men

phrases.latin: testō caldō operītō, prūnā īnsuper et circum operītō
phrases.english: cover it with a hot lid, and with embers on top and all round

sources: Lewis & Short: super · Lewis & Short: superus · Lewis & Short: insuper
